# Pragma Research

> Cadence is a novel real-time AI modeled after animal and human brains. It learns from live experience.

A typical deployed transformer keeps its learned weights fixed during use. Cadence explores an equilibrium brain that retains knowledge and can repair it from witnessed outcomes. Pragma Research builds the brains for robots that keep improving throughout their working lives. Robotics is the first proposed market. The product direction is a supported Cadence runtime and a brain prepared for a customer's embodiment, beginning with a paid evaluation on one adaptation or recovery task.

For one continuing creature, construct Brain.compose(inputs=4, actions=2, arousal=ArousalConfig()) and call brain.live(observation), then brain.live(next_observation, reward=reward) with the last action's outcome. The live loop settles calm responses without learning and admits learning when aroused. Default System 1 contains reciprocal neural regions, plastic connections, a working trace, associative memory and private responses to supplied hypothetical observations. Optional System 2 adds observing regions to a developed two-module System 1 inside that same settlement. Bounded observer-like patches carry local state and receive signals through ports; readback, retained records and local repair support the intended world model. Actual accepted outcomes or demonstrations can update it. The acquired brain persists through use.

Its intended lifecycle is bootstrap, familiar operation, witnessed mismatch, local repair and retained correction. Familiar behavior should reuse acquired knowledge at low additional cost. Brain.live supplies a first routine-and-repair loop for one stream, measured in one bounded chamber. Integrated learned world prediction, repair localized to what failed, broader retained capabilities and a measured cost advantage remain research goals. Numerical convergence does not establish correctness about the world, and mathematical energy is not electrical energy. Canonical guide: https://github.com/muellerberndt/cadence/blob/main/docs/world-model.md

- [Compared with deep learning](https://floatingpragma.io/cadence/#deep-networks): a settled equilibrium of the whole brain and local repair, beside a one-pass network trained by backpropagation.
- [Interactive brain](https://floatingpragma.io/cadence/#inside-the-brain): switch between state-coupled and observer layouts of the separate population solver, inspect patch state and error, and compare settlement with a forward calculation.

Simulation evidence establishes bounded behavior under the stated conditions. Physical robot adaptation, a useful advantage from recursive depth, broad retention and electrical energy advantages require separate tests. Evidence excerpts are compact source projections, not complete reproduction bundles.

## Research origin

Observer Patch Holography (OPH) asks whether bounded observers can build a shared physical account from local records, overlap comparison and repair. Its organizing idea inspired Cadence; cortical cooperation supplies another computational inspiration. Formal proofs establish consequences of specified assumptions. A physical or biological interpretation requires its own evidence.

- [Research overview](https://floatingpragma.io/physics/).

## Advantages for embodied AI

Cadence takes inspiration from continuing biological learning. Its local plasticity is a software mechanism, not a claim of biological equivalence. The embodied design includes:

- Learning on the job: bootstrap useful skills, then keep the acquired brain alive during use and admit actual outcomes. Brain.live supplies a bounded routine-and-repair loop; broader retention and repair localized to what failed need separate evidence.
- Adaptation to changed conditions: a worn actuator, a new payload or a different surface shows up in what the robot measures, and measured outcomes can support correction. Recovery and retained skills are separate tests.
- Local learning: each connection changes from the activity of the two units it joins; the default brain keeps no backward computation graph, so learning can run on the robot itself.
- Memory: a working trace carries the recent past and an associative memory keeps what mattered.
- Settled answers: every action is the settled state of the whole brain, and a brain that does not settle refuses to act.
- Inspection: the activity of every region can be read while the brain runs, and private imagination tests a response before the body commits to it.

The separate Rover Lab, Patch World and Atari Arcade engines demonstrate bounded parts of this design in simulation. Cadence is experimental research software; a physical robot evaluation is the next test. Conditional gradient arguments do not establish task competence or an efficiency advantage.

## Compared with a deep neural network

A feed-forward reference computes outputs through directed layers. Cadence's default brain instead forms an answer by settling a reciprocal neural graph, then uses local free/nudged activity contrasts for learning. Finite teaching remains the default; qualified teaching explicitly checks every required phase, and reward eligibility has a separate finite-phase contract. Conditional gradient arguments retain their symmetry, stable-branch and small-nudge assumptions. Conventional systems can also be recurrent or learn online. Depth and local updates do not by themselves establish better acquisition or cheaper operation. Full comparison: https://github.com/muellerberndt/cadence#how-a-cadence-brain-differs-from-a-feed-forward-network

## Brain design: System 1 and optional System 2

System 1 is the default brain, composed with Brain.compose; System 2 adds optional observers to a developed two-module System 1 in the same brain. Every answer is the settled state of the whole brain, and a brain that does not settle refuses to act. Beside the main interface, Cadence keeps advanced engines with their own contracts: the population solver, where populations of patches settle one joint energy and observers read exact prediction errors; record patches for event records and consolidation; and a temporal model for learned action consequences and planning. System 1 and System 2 name functional roles in software, not claims of biological equivalence. Choose observers by measured task quality, query latency and learning cost; deeper is not automatically better or faster. Archived AMEN uses a record-patch brain trained on an earlier release.

## Public demonstrations

The official demonstration source is https://github.com/muellerberndt/cadence-demos. The website showcase is https://floatingpragma.io/demos/.

- Atari Arcade: https://floatingpragma.io/demos/atari-arcade/ — a playable browser edition in which fresh Cadence brains learn Freeway and Atlantis from a scripted teacher and rewards, on an Atari 2600 emulator with a JavaScript version of the Cadence 0.70 System 1 brain; the Python server edition with four games is at https://github.com/muellerberndt/cadence-demos/tree/main/atari-arcade.
- AMEN: https://floatingpragma.io/demos/amen/ — a playable record-patch composer trained on Cadence 0.70; fixed learned checkpoint, generated musical events and supplied instrument.
- Patch World: https://floatingpragma.io/demos/patch-world/ — a playable JavaScript artificial-life simulation on the Cadence 0.70 population solver: brains that learn in the browser and evolve their layouts, with observer stages as an optional gene.
- Rover Lab: https://floatingpragma.io/demos/rover-lab/ — a playable browser edition of a simulated rover whose live body model adapts when a wheel weakens, with no separate training mode: a four-patch brain on a JavaScript version of the Cadence 0.70 population solver, a supplied action selector and declared timing measurements; the Python edition on cadence-net 0.70.0, with an optional observer arm, is at https://github.com/muellerberndt/cadence-demos/tree/main/rover-lab.

The embedded browser applications are copied from a pinned cadence-demos commit; their source and published file hashes are at https://floatingpragma.io/demos/runtime/manifest.json. Their engines differ, so the showcase identifies each mechanism and result separately.
